title.narrative: Greater Mekong Subregion Health Security Project

description.narrative:
The Greater Mekong Subregion (GMS) Health Security Project is composed of (i) four loans to Cambodia, the Lao PDR, Myanmar, and Viet Nam (CLMV); and (ii) a grant to the Lao PDR. The project builds on previous and ongoing interventions focusing on communicable disease control (CDC) in Cambodia, the Lao PDR, and Viet Nam; and now including Myanmar.
The impact will be GMS public health security strengthened. The outcome will be GMS health system performance with regard to health security improved. The project has three outputs.
"Output 1: Regional cooperation and communicable disease control in border areas improved.
"Output 2: National disease surveillance and outbreak response systems strengthened.
"Output 3: Laboratory services and hospital infection prevention and control improved.

description.narrative: GMS health system performance with regard to health security improved

An additional 20 provincial and district hospitals comply with national IPC criteria Progress/Status: CAM: In progress. The baseline assessment, completed in Q1 2024, found that 64 hospitals have complied with 5 of the 9 core components of the IPC tool (compliance = minimum average score of 70% for each of the 9 components on the IPC assessment tool). The 4 core components that hospitals haven't yet achieved are: • IPC program (46%): poor IPC committee function and responsibility, lack of dedicated staff • Sterilization (51%): poor infrastructure, lack of appropriate sterilization equipment • Isolation (56%): poor isolation department, even not specific or absence infrastructure as compared with the MOH CPA development guidelines • Environment healthcare facilities (69%): lack of IPC knowledge in environment and lack of hospital hygiene infrastructure
The project is supporting those hospitals as follows: • Supply Integrated-Biomedical Wastes Treatment and Disposal (Sterilwave) to 41 hospitals • Supply Steam Sterilizer (Autoclave) to 35 hospitals • Supply washing machine to 58 hospitals • Conduct TOT training and cascade training on IPC practices in health facilities
The endline assessment on IPC was conducted in Q3 2025 with completion anticipated by end of 2025. Data Source: Cambodia: IPC training and activity reports Actual value:

An additional 30 laboratories in provincial and district hospitals achieve quality and biosafety standards Progress/Status: CAM: In progress. In 2023, 11 laboratories have achieved quality standards (based on results of the National Laboratory Assessment on Quality and Biosafety; compliance = minimum 50% of total score for facilities and biosafety).
The project is supporting the laboratories as follows: • Minor repair for 50 laboratories • Procurement of laboratory equipment • Trainings on laboratory quality management • Supervision on biosafety and bio risk management practices
The endline assessment on IPC was conducted in Q3 2025 with completion anticipated by end of 2025. Data Source: Cambodia: Laboratory quality and laboratory biosafety training and assessment reports Actual value:

271 of the 381 targeted district and/or township laboratories achieve quality and biosafety standards Progress/Status: CAM: Achieved. Project management unit (PMU) and Department of Hospital Services (DHS) finalized National Laboratory Endline Assessment on Quality and Biosafety in laboratories. The assessment found that 27 laboratories got more than 50% out of total score for laboratory quality and biosafety standards (based on results of the LQMS (March 2023; compliance = minimum 50% of total score for facilities and biosafety). Construction of a provincial hospital in Tbong Khmum was completed and fully equipped in Q2 2023. Therefore, 28 hospitals have now achieved quality and biosafety standards.
VIE: Delayed. At Q3 2021 87/245d laboratories had met both the standards for laboratory quality and standards for laboratory biosafety.
Amongst the 245 target laboratories There are • 111 district laboratories have achieved the laboratory quality standards. • 137 district laboratories had attained biosafety level-II.
100 of the laboratories currently at biosafety level-I require bio-safety cabinets to allow them to be graded level-II. The project is proposing procurement of these cabinets under the project extension request. Data Source: Cambodia, Lao PDR, Myanmar: Laboratory quality and laboratory biosafety training and assessment reports

Compliance with the 8 APSED focus areas increased Progress/Status: CAM: Achieved. The 3 (baseline) APSED focus areas achieved are (i) Surveillance, risk assessment and response, (ii) Zoonosis, and (iii) Risk communication. Compliance = score of 50% or greater. As of Q1 2024 (based on results of the 2023 State Party Self-assessment Annual Reporting), 7/8ASBased on results of the 2023 State Party self-assessment Annual ReportingPSED focus areas complied with are (i) Laboratory (80%), (ii) Surveillance (90%), (iii) Infection Prevention and Control (66%), (iv) Risk communication (73%), (v) Zoonotic (60%), (vi) M&E (Achieved), and (vii) Health emergency management (57%).
LAO: Achieved. 5 out of 8 APSED focus areas increased compliance status (namely: public health emergency preparedness from 40% to 60%; laboratories from 66% to 71%; prevention through health care from 50% to 66%; risk communication from 65% to 70%; and regional preparedness, alert and response from 53% to 68%)
VIE: On track (achieved). Viet Nam has achieved 23/24 IHR indicators at level 3 or above on the IHR State Party Self-Assessment tool, equivalent to 95.8% compliance based on the 2020 assessment. This was an increase from the 2019 and 2018 assessments, in which Viet Nam had achieved 21/24 (87.5%) and 19/24 (79%) respectively. Data Source: WHO APSED report and country APSED reports Actual value:

Output: Emergency preparedness and response capacity for COVID-19 strengthened Indicator: 4h. By Q4 2024, at least 50% of ICU doctors and nurses in 14 provincial and district referral hospitals have improved knowledge on clinical management of COVID-19 (Baseline: 0, Q2 2021) Progress/Status: CAM: Achieved. By the end of 2023, 65 ICU doctors and nurses have been trained, from which 60 demonstrated improved knowledge. There are 183 ICU staff at the 14 hospitals.

Output: Emergency preparedness and response capacity for COVID-19 strengthened Indicator: 4i. By Q4 2024, 14 referral hospitals meet their oxygen-supply requirement through on-site oxygen plants (Baseline: 0, Q2 2021) Progress/Status: CAM: Achieved. Output: Emergency preparedness and response capacity for COVID-19 strengthened Indicator: 4j. By Q4 2024, at least 50% of frontline health care workers in 14 provincial hospitals have increased knowledge on support and referral measures for survivors of GBV (Baseline: 0; Q2 2021) Progress/Status: CAM: Achieved. Frontline health workers, in this context, refer to outpatient health staff and those specifically responsible for providing mental health, psychosocial, and gender-based violence services to persons affected by these issues. A total of158 (83 females) frontline health workers in 14 provincial hospitals.
As of 30 September, 2025, the project successfully conducted six training sessions on Support and Referral Measures for Survivors of GBV and Persons Affected by Mental Health and Psychosocial Issues, reaching a total of 114 front-line health staff (71=62% female) from 14 provincial hospitals. Pre- and post-test assessments demonstrated a significant increase in knowledge among all participants regarding referral measures for survivors of GBV and the identification and treatment of persons affected by mental health conditions. This achievement exceeds the project's target of at least 50% of front-line health workers having increased knowledge, as 114 out of 158 total front-line health staff (72%) now have a better understanding. Data Source: Pre- and post- training assessments Actual value:

Output: Laboratory services and hospital IPC improved Indicator: 3d. By 2025, 50 targeted laboratories have been audited at least once for quality and biosafety (Baseline: 0; Q2 2021) Progress/Status: CAM: Achieved. In 2023 the baseline laboratory audit was conducted in 64 laboratories using the LQMS tool. The audit revealed that 59 of 64 laboratories (92%) were classified at Level 1, 2 laboratories (3%) at Level 3, 2 laboratories (3%) at Level 4, and 1 laboratory (2%) at Level 5. No laboratories were classified at Level 2 or Level 6. Data Source: Laboratory audit reports Actual value:

Output: Laboratory services and hospital IPC improved Indicator: 3e. By 2025, 2 staff members (at least one of them female) in each of 50 targeted laboratories s, t, u trained in national laboratory biosafety standards and practice (Baseline: 0; Q2 2021) Progress/Status: CAM: Achieved. In 2024, three Basic Biosafety and Biosecurity (BASIC) training sessions were conducted for 102 laboratory staff (including 27 female staff) from 27 of the 50 targeted laboratories.
In Q3 2025, two additional training sessions were organized, reaching 92 staff (including 31 female staff) and prioritizing laboratories that had not previously received training to ensure participation of at least one female staff member from each site.
Cumulatively, 194 laboratory staff (including 58 female staff) from all 50 targeted laboratories have been trained, achieving full coverage. These trainings have enhanced biosafety and biosecurity standards and practices across the participating laboratories.
Data Source: Laboratory biosafety training and assessment reports Actual value:

Output: National disease surveillance and outbreak response systems strengthened Indicator: 2a. By 2024, 213 districts and/or townships send sex-disaggregated electronic report on communicable diseases as per national regulations Progress/Status: CAM: Achieved. All health facilities under 52 ODs covered by project are reporting to the Health Information System (HIS).
The HIS contains information on routine health service activities and health data including communicable diseases from all levels of the national healthcare system. In 2009, additional gender and vertical program data were included in the system. All health facilities to capture monthly data into their respective reporting forms (HC1 for Health Centers and HO2 for Hospitals) through the web-based system within 15 days after month end.
LAO: Achieved. Currently all outbreak data are sex disaggregated. Disease information sharing continue among CLMV countries
VIE: On Track - Achieved target At Q3 2021 all districts reported sex-disaggregated case data through the e-CDS 100% (245/245) of DHCs have had staff trained in the use of infectious disease reporting software following the requirements of Circular 54/2015/TT-BYT, including reporting of sex disaggregated data. Data Source: 2a. District and/or township disease surveillance electronic reports Actual value:

Output: National disease surveillance and outbreak response systems strengthened Indicator: 2b. By 2024, 80% of major outbreak response reports indicate appropriate measure conducted (2015 baseline estimate: 60%) Progress/Status: CAM: Achieved. In 2018, 2019 and 2020, all outbreak response reports (100%) indicate appropriate measure. Appropriate measure refers report follows CDC department surveillance and response SOPs: (i) Detect cluster, (ii) verify clusters, (iii) Conduct risk assessment, (iv). Form outbreak response team, (v) Written report (Primary report, descriptive report or scientific report).
LAO: Achieved. During HSP, out of 126 outbreaks, 110 (87%) reported within 24 hours; 105 (83%) investigated within 24-48 hours; and 100% are compliant with RRT SOP
VIE: On Track - Achieved target Data is collated annually. In Q3 2021, 22 provinces reported a total of 1592 outbreaks, 1582 (99%) of which were managed within the timeframe specified in MOH regulations. In 2020 99% (4,635/4,644) of outbreaks requiring management were done so within the timeframe specified in MOH regulations.
In 2019, 99% (11,165 / 11,258) of outbreaks were managed within the required timeframe. Data Source: 2b. Annual provincial and/or township reports Actual value:

Output: National disease surveillance and outbreak response systems strengthened Indicator: 2c. By 2025, electronic reporting system for COVID-19, with case data disaggregated by sex, established and in routine use in 24 provinces and Phnom Penh municipality as per national regulations (Baseline: NA; Q2 2021) Progress/Status: CAM: Achieved. The electronic reporting system for COVID-19 is being recorded the case data disaggregated by sex on daily basis. The published report is following WHO standard. The MOH COVID-19 Surveillance Report demonstrates the achievement of this indicator. The report confirms that the electronic COVID-19 reporting system is fully operational and routinely used by all 24 provinces and Phnom Penh Municipality, with case data disaggregated by sex, in accordance with national regulations. This provides clear evidence that the indicator establishment and routine use of the electronic reporting system has been met. The reporting system available at http://www.cdcmoh.gov.kh/ Data Source: MOH/DCDC monthly summary reports Baseline year: 2021 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2021 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Regional cooperation and CDC in border areas improved Indicator: 1a. By 2020, Cambodia, the Lao PDR, Myanmar, and Viet Nam apply harmonized standard case definitions, and reporting procedures for notifiable communicable diseases (baseline: NA), including disaggregation by sex and age Progress/Status: CAM: Achieved. All countries agreed to follow WHO standard case definitions which mentioned in the IHR. Cambodia provide the report of 7 epidemic prone diseases and syndromes on weekly basis which posted on CDC department website http://cdcmoh.gov.kh/surveillance/camewarn.
LAO: Achieved. LAO uses standard WHO case definitions and has 18 notifiable diseases as well as EWARN reporting. Disease Information Exchange between CMV identifies 13 agreed core diseases and outbreaks are reported weekly and monthly between the countries.
VIE: On-track. At the mid-term review the indicator was clarified, whereby ‘harmonized case definitions' was defined as “case-definition based on WHO case definitions, modified for country context.”
In Viet Nam 9 Group A infectious diseases have case definitions that are harmonized with WHO case definitions.
Regional reporting follows the procedures for reporting to WHO in IHR Annex 2. PMU Viet Nam will coordinate with the ADB regional public health consultant to confirm diseases for which WHO case definitions are commonly applied by the four project countries. Data Source: 1a. WHO standard case definition for infectious diseasesf and International Health Regulations Annex 2 for standard reporting procedure for 7 priority notifiable diseases in the GMS Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2021 Target value: 100

Output: Regional cooperation and CDC in border areas improved Indicator: 1b. By 2021, all border provinces, states, or regions targeted by the project conduct two cross-border activities per year Progress/Status: CAM: Achieved. By 2021 all 14 border provinces were conducted at least two activities with neighboring border provinces.
In 2021 the activities were focused on information sharing and cooperation (e.g. on border quarantine) on COVID-19 response.
Cross border meeting (province to province) including 14 project provinces have been organized under governor's authority to discuss on how to respond with COVID-19 pandemic at the border areas.
All 14 project provinces shared information on disease outbreak (COVID-19) with Lao PDR, Vietnam and Thailand. (100%).
LAO: Partially achieved and on track. COVID-19 restrictions in 2020 and 2021 interrupted many cross border events and activities. During COVID-19, the project organised cross border meetings at border checkpoints to circumvent restrictions and to continue liaison and coordination with neighbouring countries and counterparts
VIE: Delayed. In 2019, 6 of the 12 target provincese implemented a total of 11 cross border activities. In addition, one non-target province bordering PRC (Cao Bang) implemented 2 cross-border activities. From Q1 2020 to Q3 2021 priority provinces have had limited opportunity to implement cross-border activities due to COVID-19 restrictions. Ha Tinh Province implemented one information sharing activity in Q3 2021. Data Source: 1b.
